citations.quote: Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
Every ordinal $\alpha \in \omega_1$ is at most countable

derivations.claim: The double-stick sequence is countably infinite, and recursive selections inside X have distinct stick indices and distinct defined infinite-intersection indices.
inputs: only countably many earlier countable sets are excluded at each stage

derivations.claim: One double-stick set lies inside X and has infinite remainder after every finite union of the prescribed almost-disjoint sequence.
inputs: finite almost-coverage forces infinitely many distinct zeta_i into the same finite index set

derivations.claim: The recursive array is defined at every ordinal; limit rows are assigned either distinct selections from infinite Y sets or split cofinal ladders.
inputs: finite prior choices at each natural stage j; simultaneous ordinal enumerations and ladders

derivations.claim: The completed sequence A_alpha has pairwise finite intersections and disjoint cofinal members in each limit row.
inputs: a good upper row excludes each earlier A_beta from all selections past one finite index; a ladder meets smaller ordinals finitely

derivations.claim: The strengthened double-stick property gives tail-contained robust witnesses, whose index-and-element closure set D_X is club.
inputs: omega-stage closure and the direct limit-point test

derivations.claim: Every delta in D_X is good and every row member guesses X cofinally.
inputs: pi pairs a witness index with the desired row member, and the chosen point lies above an arbitrary b

derivations.claim: Diagonal intersection provides every target index below delta on a club, hence stationary simultaneous guesses on every part of P.
inputs: regularity of omega_1; stationarity persists after club intersection
